project.title: Primary settling changes the microbial community of influent wastewater to wastewater treatment plants
project.description: The continuous immigration of bacteria in influent wastewater strongly impacts the microbial community of activated sludge (AS) in wastewater treatment plants (WWTP), both in terms of species composition and abundance. Therefore, it is of interest to elucidate the route of immigrating bacteria into the biological tanks, including the effect of primary settlers. These are commonly used pretreatment units that can potentially selectively increase or reduce the relative abundance of certain bacteria. Species-level identification of the microbial composition of influent wastewater before and after primary settling was carried out in four full-scale municipal WWTPs biweekly over one year by 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Primary settling significantly affected the microbial composition of the influent wastewater immigrating to the biological tanks. Overall, 37-49% of incoming COD was removed in the primary settlers. Most genera and species were present in the wastewater of all four plants and the trend of these were investigated across the primary settlers. Approx 50% of the genera had the same trend across at least three WWTPs. Few genera significantly increased in relative read abundance (3.7%) after settling, while 22.3% showed a significant reduction in relative abundance. In particular, we investigated process-critical species in AS, such as known nitrifiers, polyphosphate-accumulating organisms, and filamentous bacteria. Most taxa were affected similarly in all WWTPs including multiple genera involved in bulking in AS. However, some genera, e.g. important polyphosphate-accumulating bacteria, had inconsistent trends across WWTPs, suggesting that the characteristics of the wastewater are important for the trend of some bacteria through primary settling. In all cases, primary settling changed the microbial community of the influent wastewater, posing an obvious candidate for upstream control to optimize the assembly of the microbial communities in activated sludge.
